title: White Temple and Anu Ziggurat, Uruk
summary: The White Temple at Uruk, southern Iraq, is a hall about 22 by 17.5 m standing on a mudbrick terrace raised at least ten times to about 12 m, the Anu Ziggurat. Radiocarbon dates the building to 3517–3358 BCE, making it the earliest preserved temple on a ziggurat.

uncertainty.note: Range is the radiocarbon span for erection of the building quoted by Artefacts Berlin; a conservation report says built around 3500 BC. The terrace was raised and extended repeatedly.

where.modern_name: White Temple, Anu Ziggurat, Uruk (Warka), Al-Muthanna Governorate, Iraq
where.historical_name: Anu district of Uruk (Unug), southern Mesopotamia, Late Uruk period

importance.justification: Oldest known temple preserved on a raised platform, an early step toward the ziggurat tradition.
